title: An Algorithm-Hardware Co-design Based on Revised Microscaling Format Quantization for Accelerating Large Language Models
problem: Microscaling (MX) format offers promise as drop-in FP32 replacement but lacks practical hardware support; dominant low-precision LLM inference still relies on low-bit quantization, limiting scalability of MX format deployment.
motivation: MX format enables efficient narrow-bit inference but requires co-designed hardware; current absence of MX accelerators prevents widespread adoption despite algorithmic advantages.
method: Algorithm-hardware co-design with two levels: (1) RMFQ (Revised MX Format Quantization) introduces revised MX (RMX) format with novel group direction strategy for improved quantization; (2) RMFA (Revised MX Format Accelerator) implements RMX-adaptive hardware architecture and RMX encoding scheme optimized for low-bit operations.
key_novelty: Revised MX format with group direction strategy and dedicated hardware accelerator achieves state-of-the-art 4-bit and 6-bit quantization with practical deployment viability.
contributions: Revised MX (RMX) format with novel group direction quantization strategy
RMFQ quantization framework pushing 4-bit and 6-bit to state-of-the-art
RMFA hardware architecture with RMX-adaptive design and encoding scheme
1.28x speedup and 1.31x energy reduction vs outlier-aware accelerators
primary_theme: Revised MX format with co-designed hardware for 4-6 bit LLM inference
